 Print The recent episode of Bigg Boss 20 witnessed a heated argument between Manish Goel and Qazi Touqeer during the nomination round. Manish, who had earlier made it clear that he disliked being called a 'Professor', lost his cool when Qazi once again addressed him by the same name. The duo had a major showdown during the nomination round. Later, he broke down in tears while recalling one of the darkest phases of his life after Qazi triggered painful memories from his school days. During the conversation, Manish said he was reminded of an incident that took place when he was between 12 and 14 years old, describing it as something he has tried to bury and never revisit. “It's the darkest phase of my life. School time. It is something which I don't want to dig that grave ever,” Manish said. He went on to explain to Gullu, Love Gill and Kanika Mann, that he felt Qazi had deliberately touched upon something deeply personal that triggered him. “Today I realised he used it as a trigger. My mistake. I shouldn't have got triggered. He got that consent from that trigger. He got what he wanted,” he said. The conversation took an emotional turn when Manish referred to something that happened when he was in eighth, ninth or 10th standard. He suggested that his mother and Poonam know what he went through, but added that he usually prefers not to discuss it. Manish opens up about his painful past
 “I was only about 12, 13 or probably 14. Some things you just dig forever. It's very dark. I try not to think about it at all,” he said. When asked to sum up what happened during that period, Manish, visibly emotional, said: “In only one word, I tried committing suicide.” Join conversation

 He then attempted to end the conversation about the painful memory and made it clear that it was extremely difficult for him to revisit that chapter of his life. The incident took place after Qazi appeared to connect Manish's comments about being a “professor” and a “good-looking man” with the traumatic period he had referred to. Manish revealed that the subject was linked to his experiences during his school years.
